subject: Proposal: Tiered Reserved Capacity Options & Ramp Safeguards
messages:
From: Sarah Burns <sarah.burns@vitalpath.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-14T16:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask — reserved capacity and ramp constraints

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo Friday. VitalPath is close to selecting a partner for inference hosting, and our procurement team asked for a short write-up with commitment options tied to predictable latency and predictable unit cost. Our key constraints are: 1) steady-state 1500 concurrent requests per minute at p95 <= 200ms for 1k token responses, 2) a plan to scale to 3x within 6 months, and 3) a strict data residency requirement for US-East.

Can you send a proposal that outlines cluster sizing choices, suggested minimum GPUs (and how that maps to throughput), ramp schedule options with soft/hard guardrails, and any warm-start / pre-warm credits you can include for go-live? We also need an estimate of activation lead time per tranche for contract and ops.

Sarah
Sarah Burns
Head of Platform Integrations — VitalPath Health
Attachments: vitalpath_requirements_v1.pdf (PDF stub, 142KB)
From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Burns <sarah.burns@vitalpath.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-15T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — reserved capacity and ramp constraints

Hi Sarah — great to connect. Per below is an initial, pragmatic set of options we recommend for VitalPath based on the traffic profile and residency requirement. I'll attach a worksheet with throughput estimates and cost buckets. High-level summary first, then details.

Summary options (all US-East, SLA-backed lanes):

- Option A (Conservative baseline): 24 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv), min active 18 GPUs, target steady-state throughput ~1.2k concurrent RPS-equivalent, p95 ~170ms. Activation lead time: 7 business days.
- Option B (Balanced ramp): 36 GPUs, min active 24 GPUs, steady-state ~2.0k concurrent, p95 ~150ms. Activation lead time: 10 business days for first tranche, subsequent tranches 5 days.
- Option C (Aggressive buffer + burst): 60 GPUs, min active 36 GPUs, supports immediate 3x headroom and bursting; p95 ~130ms with regional warm warm pools. Activation lead time: 18 business days.

Ramp scheduling patterns we recommend (pick one):

1) Staircase (recommended for predictable spend): start at Option A min active, jump to B after 45 days, move to C only after sustained usage over 60 days.
2) Fast-phase (for growth targets): start at B, commit to additional 12 GPUs at month 2, full C at month 4.
3) Burst-enabled (for marketing spikes): maintain B baseline with pre-configured burst-to-C for up to 72 hours per month; burst usage billed at lower committed rate but with overage guardrails.

Warm-start / pre-warm credits: we can include two weeks of pre-warm credits for the initial go-live (covers traffic shaping, KV cache priming, and scheduled load tests).

Attachments: reserve_options_spreadsheet.xlsx (XLSX stub) — includes per-GPU throughput modeling, expected token cost, and latency curves by sequence length.

Next steps: if you prefer, we can map these to a mutual action plan and indicate the point at which we’ll enable dedicated routing, private VPC peering, and audit logs for SOC-type evidence.

Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the worksheet.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, Sarah Burns <sarah.burns@vitalpath.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — reserved capacity and ramp constraints

Quick follow-up on Priyom's options — two notes from an ops/serving perspective:

- Min active GPUs vs. licensing: For the numbers above, min active is what we need for latency SLOs given the model family and 1k token tails. If VitalPath wants to reduce keep-warm cost, we can propose a soft-min (auto-warm within 30 minutes) with slightly higher p95 during cold windows.
- Warm-start sequencing: recommend a staged KV cache priming plan that runs across 48 hours with incremental traffic mirroring. This reduces peak cold-start token cost and avoids sudden burst throttles in the first 72 hours.

Also tagging a possible middle-ground SKU: 48 GPUs, min active 30 — effectively reduces cost vs C but gives better burst headroom than B.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Burns <sarah.burns@vitalpath.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T11:06:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — reserved capacity and ramp constraints

Adding timeline constraints from onboarding and compliance:

- VPC peering + billing sign-off typically needs 5–7 business days after legal/compliance sign-off.
- SOC/PCI evidence packaging takes 3 business days once we get their list of required artifacts.
- For Option C activation (60 GPUs) we need a minimum 10 business-day runway to reserve capacity on our side and schedule any dedicated provisioning windows.

I'll prepare a short activation checklist (networking, secrets/KMS, audit hooks, smoke tests) to include in the MLP (mutual launch plan).

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Burns <sarah.burns@vitalpath.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@vitalpath.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — reserved capacity and ramp constraints

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement asked for. A couple quick questions before we map to a deal: 1) for Option B with a 24 GPU min active, is there an SLA credit if p95 breaches 250ms during peak for more than 3 hours in a 30-day window? 2) can you confirm whether the pre-warm credits can be applied to smoke tests that run from our CI pipeline (yes/no)? 3) please add the 48-GPU middle-ground option to the sheet and a one-line note on expected monthly burn delta vs B.

If you can update the worksheet and list the exact activation lead times per tranche we can share with procurement and get an initial purchase order out. Can we target sending that back by EOD Thursday?

Best,
Sarah
